<!-- Generated by go run ./internal/conn3x/provider/moddoc in conn3xorg/conn3x. Don't edit by hand. -->

Holds a package back from updates, or releases it: apt-mark hold on Debian and Ubuntu, dnf versionlock on the Red Hat family. It doesn't install the package.

Use `package_hold` to keep a package at the version it has while the rest of the host updates, such as the kernel on a host with a driver built for it, or a database you upgrade by hand. It's `apt-mark hold` on Debian and Ubuntu and `dnf versionlock` on the Red Hat family. It doesn't install anything: put a [`package`](package.md) step first if the package isn't there yet.

## Example usage

Hold PostgreSQL where it is. Steps run in the order written, so the hold comes after the install:

```hcl
step "postgres" {
  package {
    name = "postgresql16-server"
  }
}

step "postgres_held" {

  package_hold {
    name = "postgresql16-server"
  }
}
```

On Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux and RHEL, `dnf versionlock` is a plugin. Install it first:

```hcl
step "versionlock" {
  package {
    name = "python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock"
  }
}
```

Let it update again, when you're ready:

```hcl
step "postgres_held" {
  package_hold {
    name  = "postgresql16-server"
    state = "released"
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | Package name, such as kernel or postgresql16-server. |
| `on_remove` | string | No | What happens on the host when this resource is removed: "forget" (default) leaves the hold as it is, "delete" releases it. |
| `state` | string | No | "held" (default) keeps the package at its version through updates; "released" lets it update again. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_package_hold.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the package was held, or released, as it should be at the last refresh. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_package_hold` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.

## How it works

**Holding.** On the Debian family, Conn3x runs `apt-mark hold`, and `apt-mark unhold` to release. On the Red Hat family it runs `dnf versionlock add`, which locks the installed version, and `dnf versionlock delete` to release. A hold needs the package installed: holding one that isn't fails and says to install it first, since there's no version to hold, and releasing one that isn't is fine. After the command, Conn3x reads the list back, because `dnf versionlock` exits 0 even for a name it can't find, as with a typo. Fedora's dnf 5 has `versionlock` built in. dnf 4, on Rocky Linux 10, AlmaLinux and RHEL, needs `python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock`, and without it the step fails and names that package.

**Reading.** Every plan reads `apt-mark showhold` or `dnf versionlock list`. A hold someone released by hand, or one someone added, shows the step out of sync, and the next apply puts it back the way the step says. Apply changes nothing when the host already matches.

**What a hold does.** `apt upgrade` and `dnf upgrade` leave a held package at its version, so a routine update, by hand, by `unattended-upgrades` or by `dnf-automatic`, can't move it. To move it on purpose, release it, upgrade, and hold it again.

## Removal

Deleting a `package_hold` step leaves the hold as it is. With `on_remove = "delete"`, it releases it.
